          h2 "Long-running serverless apps"
          p "Durable objects run for as long as the work takes. They can compute in the background and handle high volumes of requests concurrently."
      [marketing-card-grid-cell]
        [marketing-topic icon=true described=true]
          h2 "Every user in sync, instantly"
          p "Each durable object works as a WebSocket server and client. Broadcast state to all connected clients in a few lines of code."
      [marketing-card-grid-cell]
        [marketing-topic icon=true described=true]
          h2 "Scale to millions as you grow"
          p "Give each unit of work in your app its own lightweight, isolated durable object. Run millions of them, with no capacity to plan."
      [marketing-card-grid-cell]
        [marketing-topic icon=true described=true]
          h2 "Durable state, no lost writes"
          p "Every durable object has an embedded SQLite database, so state survives restarts and failures. No write is confirmed until it's durable."
      [marketing-card-grid-cell]
        [marketing-topic icon=true described=true]
          h2 "Background work on autopilot"
          p "Run code in the background, poll APIs periodically, or schedule future work with alarms. The platform wakes the durable object on time."
      [marketing-card-grid-cell]
        [marketing-topic icon=true described=true]
          h2 "Ship faster with no rewrites"
          p "Use the Durable Objects API you already know. Existing classes run on Azion without a rewrite, so you write the logic, not the plumbing."

        h2 "One coordinator for every unit of shared state"
        p "Every call to a durable object reaches its one active instance, wherever it runs across 100+ data centers. A conditional write in durable storage guarantees a single owner, even during network failures. You write the class. Azion handles placement, routing, and failover."

  · section-gap (hatched spacer band)
  [block-use-case-links aria-label='Use cases']
    [marketing-section-module kind=left]
      [marketing-section-title kind=left size=medium]
        h2 "Use cases"
      [marketing-card-grid kind=divider columns=3 mobile-columns=1 filled=true]
        [marketing-topic icon=true described=true]
          h3 "Stateful agent runtime"
          p "Give each agent its own durable object to keep conversation and task state, run steps in order, and resume after a pause."
        [marketing-topic icon=true described=true]
          h3 "Real-time chat with presence"
          p "Run one durable object per room to store messages, track who's online, and broadcast every update to connected users."
        [marketing-topic icon=true described=true]
          h3 "Authoritative game server"
          p "Keep each match's players, rules, and score in one durable object and push every move to all players as it happens."
        [marketing-topic icon=true described=true]
          h3 "Live document sync"
          p "Route all edits to a document through its durable object, so concurrent changes apply in order and everyone sees the same version."
        [marketing-topic icon=true described=true]
          h3 "Inventory and seat reservations"
          p "Manage each event, cart, or SKU in its own durable object, so the same seat or item is never sold or added twice."
        [marketing-topic icon=true described=true]
          h3 "Consistent shared counters"
          p "Count likes, votes, views, or quotas in a durable object, so every increment lands even when updates arrive all at once."

  [block-code-split]
    [marketing-section-module kind=left]
      [marketing-media-split kind=media-end orientation=horizontal size=medium align=top media=true divided=true fill=canvas aria-label='The shortest path to real-time, stateful apps']
        h2 "The shortest path to real-time, stateful apps"
        p "Requests from anywhere reach the same durable object, so one instance coordinates every client that shares its state. It handles fan-in and fan-out over WebSockets, and its embedded SQLite database keeps state, events, and history next to your code."
        [code-code-block]
          button "counter.ts"
          button "chat.ts"
          button "agent.ts"
          text "counter.ts"
          icon-button "Copy the code sample"
          text: import ⏎ DurableObject ⏎ from ⏎ 'azion/durable-objects' ⏎ export ⏎ class ⏎ Counter ⏎ extends ⏎ DurableObject ⏎ // Events run one at a time: two increments never interleave. ⏎ async ⏎ increment ⏎ () ⏎ const ⏎ next ⏎ (( ⏎ await ⏎ this ⏎ ctx ⏎ storage ⏎ get ⏎ 'count' ⏎ )) ⏎ ?? 0) + 1; ⏎ await ⏎ this ⏎ ctx ⏎ storage ⏎ put ⏎ 'count' ⏎ next ⏎ ); ⏎ return ⏎ next ⏎ export ⏎ default ⏎ async ⏎ fetch ⏎ request ⏎ env ⏎ const ⏎ name ⏎ new ⏎ URL ⏎ request ⏎ url ⏎ ). ⏎ searchParams ⏎ get ⏎ 'name' ⏎ ); ⏎ if ⏎ !name) ⏎ return ⏎ new ⏎ Response ⏎ 'Missing ?name' ⏎ status ⏎ }); ⏎ const ⏎ total ⏎ await ⏎ env ⏎ COUNTER ⏎ get ⏎ env ⏎ COUNTER ⏎ idFromName ⏎ name ⏎ )). ⏎ increment ⏎ (); ⏎ return ⏎ Response ⏎ json ⏎ ({ ⏎ name ⏎ total ⏎ }); ⏎ };
